# nginx — 2026 high-value CVEs (CVSS>=7, CISA KEV, Exploit-DB, or SSVC exploitation active/poc)

Full records for all 112 nginx CVEs of 2026 are in `data/cve/vendors/nginx/2026.jsonl`.

### CVE-2026-1580 — ingress-nginx auth-method nginx configuration injection
- Assigner: kubernetes | Published: 2026-02-03 | Updated: 2026-02-26 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper Input Validation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A security issue was discovered in ingress-nginx where the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-method` Ingress annotation can be used to inject configuration into nginx. This can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the ingress-nginx controller, and disclosure of Secrets accessible to the controller. (Note that in the default installation, the controller can access all Secrets cluster-wide.)

Affected:
- Kubernetes / ingress-nginx: affected 0 <1.13.7 (semver); affected 0 <1.14.3 (semver)

Credits: Volcengine Security Team

References:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136677

- CWE: CWE-349 CWE-349: Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

A vulnerability exists in NGINX OSS and NGINX Plus when configured to proxy to upstream Transport Layer Security (TLS) servers. An attacker with a man-in-the-middle (MITM) position on the upstream server side—along with conditions beyond the attacker's control—may be able to inject plain text data into the response from an upstream proxied server.  Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

A vulnerability was identified in cym1102 nginxWebUI up to 4.3.7. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file /adminPage/conf/check of the component Web Management Interface. Such manipulation of the argument nginxDir leads to cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

### CVE-2026-8711 — NGINX JavaScript vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-05-19 | Updated: 2026-05-21 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122 Heap-based Buffer Overflow
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

NGINX JavaScript has a vulnerability when the js_fetch_proxy directive is configured with at least one client-controlled NGINX variable (for example, $http_*, $arg_*, $cookie_*) and a location invoking the ngx.fetch() operation from NGINX JavaScript. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. 


Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX JavaScript: affected 0.9.4 <0.9.9 (custom)

Credits: "F5 acknowledges udolemi (S2W) for bringing this issue to our attention and following the highest standards of coordinated disclosure."

### CVE-2026-9256 — NGINX ngx_http_rewrite_module vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-05-22 | Updated: 2026-08-25 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122 Heap-based Buffer Overflow; CWE-122 Heap-based Buffer Overflow
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_rewrite_module module. This vulnerability exists when a rewrite directive uses a regex pattern with distinct, overlapping Perl-Compatible Regular Expression (PCRE) captures (for example, ^/((.*))$) and a replacement string that references multiple such captures (for example, $1$2) in a redirect or arguments context. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. 


Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

### CVE-2026-11311 — NGINX Gateway Fabric vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-06-17 | Updated: 2026-06-17 | Max CVSS: 8.6
- CWE: CWE-76 CWE-76 Improper Neutralization of Equvalent Special Elements
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.6 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

When NGINX Plus is configured as the data plane for NGINX Gateway Fabric, an injection vulnerability exists in the NGINX configuration generator component of NGINX Gateway Fabric. User-supplied string values from the NginxProxy Custom Resource Definition serverTokens field and the AuthenticationFilter Custom Resource Definition extraAuthArgs field are rendered directly into NGINX configuration templates without sanitization or escaping. An authenticated attacker with permission to create or modify these Custom Resource Definitions may craft values that inject arbitrary NGINX configuration directives. This is a control plane issue; there is no data plane exposure from the vulnerability trigger itself. 


Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX Gateway Fabric: affected 2.5.0 <2.6.4 (custom)

Credits: F5

References:
- https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000161611 [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-15176 — NGINX ngx_http_core_module vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-10-14 | Updated: 2026-10-15 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122 Heap-based Buffer Overflow
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A vulnerability exists in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when a location is configured that uses the alias directive together with rewrite and a set or return directive referencing the $request_filename variable. Alternatively, the same result could be achieved when the $request_filename variable is used in an access log format directive. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** Avoid using alias in a location.
Avoid using the $request_filename variable.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX Plus: affected 37.1.0 <37.1.0.1 (custom); affected 37.0.0 <37.0.5.1 (custom); affected R36 <* (custom); affected R35 <* (custom); affected R34 <* (custom); affected R33 <* (custom)
- F5 / NGINX Open Source: affected 1.31.0 <1.31.7 (semver); affected 0.1.29 <1.30.6 (semver)

Credits: F5

### CVE-2026-18329 — NGINX ngx_http_js_module vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-09-02 | Updated: 2026-09-02 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-636 CWE-636
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Description

NGINX JavaScript (njs) and QuickJS (qjs) engines have a vulnerability when a js_access handler performs asynchronous request body processing and an exception is thrown during asynchronous access-control evaluation before an explicit access denial is returned. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request that triggers an error condition in the access validation logic. This may cause the js_access phase to fail open, allowing the request to proceed instead of being denied, resulting in an authentication or authorization bypass and unauthorized access to protected resources.

Impact

This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to bypass js_access controls. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** *  To secure your NGINX njs js_access handler against unhandled exceptions such as JSON.parse failures, wrap your logic in a robust try/catch block with a default strict deny policy that returns an HTML 403 Forbidden response code. For example:async function auth(r) {
  try {
    // 1. Guard input: Safely check for the Authorization header
    var authHeader = r.headersIn ? r.headersIn.Authorization : undefined;
    if (!authHeader) {
      r.warn("Access Denied: Missing Authorization header.");
      return r.return(401);
    }
    // 2. Perform the async HTTP request
    let reply = await ngx.fetch(' http://authsvc/check ', {
      headers: { Authorization: authHeader }
    });
    // 3. Validate response status
    if (reply.status !== 200) {
      r.warn(`Access Denied: Auth service returned status ${reply.status}`);
      return r.return(401);
    }
    // 4. Read response body
    // Note: ngx.fetch body is read asynchronously using .text() or .json()
    let responseText = await reply.text();
    let payload = {};
    // 5. Guard JSON.parse explicitly
    try {
      payload = JSON.parse(responseText);
    } catch (jsonError) {
      r.error(`Security Warning: Failed to parse auth service JSON payload: ${jsonError.message}`);
      // Explicitly deny the request due to malformed auth response payload
      return r.return(403);
    }
    // 6. Validate the contents of the parsed JSON
    if (payload.authorized !== true) {
      r.warn("Access Denied: Client token validated but not authorized.");
      return r.return(403);
    }
    // 7. Success: Explicitly allow the request to proceed
    return r.return(200);
  } catch (globalError) {
    // 8. Global Catch-All: Block the bypass vulnerability on any script exception
    r.error(`Security Critical: Unhandled exception in auth handler: ${globalError.toString()}`);
    // Always return 403 (Deny) on exception to guarantee a fail-closed state.
    return r.return(403);
  }
}
export default { auth };


  *  Place a security enforcement layer such as F5 WAF for NGINX or BIG-IP Advanced WAF before NGINX njs to prevent malformed requests. Configure the WAF to do the following:  *  Validate JSON syntax Enforce request body limits Block malformed payloads
  *  Reject unexpected content types Apply API schema validation

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX JavaScript: affected 1.0.0 <1.0.1 (custom); affected 0.9.9 <* (custom)

Credits: F5 acknowledges Ta Duc Thien (@thientd) of NTCS for bringing this issue to our attention and following the highest standards of coordinated disclosure.

References:
- https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000162599 [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-21441 — urllib3 vulnerable to decompression-bomb safeguard bypass when following HTTP redirects (streaming API)
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-01-07 | Updated: 2026-11-10 | Max CVSS: 8.9
- CWE: CWE-409 CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification); CWE-409 Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.9 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

urllib3 is an HTTP client library for Python. urllib3's streaming API is designed for the efficient handling of large HTTP responses by reading the content in chunks, rather than loading the entire response body into memory at once. urllib3 can perform decoding or decompression based on the HTTP `Content-Encoding` header (e.g., `gzip`, `deflate`, `br`, or `zstd`). When using the streaming API, the library decompresses only the necessary bytes, enabling partial content consumption. Starting in version 1.22 and prior to version 2.6.3, for HTTP redirect responses, the library would read the entire response body to drain the connection and decompress the content unnecessarily. This decompression occurred even before any read methods were called, and configured read limits did not restrict the amount of decompressed data. As a result, there was no safeguard against decompression bombs. A malicious server could exploit this to trigger excessive resource consumption on the client. Applications and libraries are affected when they stream content from untrusted sources by setting `preload_content=False` when they do not disable redirects. Users should upgrade to at least urllib3 v2.6.3, in which the library does not decode content of redirect responses when `preload_content=False`. If upgrading is not immediately possible, disable redirects by setting `redirect=False` for requests to untrusted source.

Affected:
- urllib3 / urllib3: affected >= 1.22, < 2.6.3
- Red Hat / Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10: unaffected 0:1.26.19-2.el10_1.1 <* (rpm)
- Red Hat / Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support: unaffected 0:1.26.19-2.el10_0.1 <* (rpm)

### CVE-2026-24512 — ingress-nginx auth-method nginx configuration injection
- Assigner: kubernetes | Published: 2026-02-03 | Updated: 2026-03-09 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper Input Validation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A security issue was discovered in ingress-nginx where the `rules.http.paths.path` Ingress field can be used to inject configuration into nginx. This can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the ingress-nginx controller, and disclosure of Secrets accessible to the controller. (Note that in the default installation, the controller can access all Secrets cluster-wide.)

Affected:
- Kubernetes / ingress-nginx: affected 0 <1.13.7 (semver); affected 0 <1.14.3 (semver)

Credits: Maxime Escourbiac and Yassine Bengana (Michelin CERT)

References:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136678

- CWE: CWE-476 CWE-476 NULL Pointer Dereference; CWE-476 NULL Pointer Dereference
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### CVE-2026-27654 — NGINX ngx_http_dav_module vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-03-24 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122: Heap-based Buffer Overflow; CWE-120 Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H`

NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_dav_module module that might allow an attacker to trigger a buffer overflow to the NGINX worker process; this vulnerability may result in termination of the NGINX worker process or modification of source or destination file names outside the document root. This issue affects NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus when the configuration file uses DAV module MOVE or COPY methods, prefix location (nonregular expression location configuration), and alias directives. The integrity impact is constrained because the NGINX worker process user has low privileges and does not have access to the entire system. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX Open Source: affected 1.29.0 <1.29.7 (semver); affected 0.5.13 <1.28.3 (semver)

### CVE-2026-27784 — NGINX ngx_http_mp4_module vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-03-24 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 8.5
- CWE: CWE-190 CWE-190 Integer Overflow or Wraparound; CWE-190 Integer Overflow or Wraparound
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.5 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

The 32-bit implementation of NGINX Open Source has a vulnerability in the ngx_http_mp4_module module, which might allow an attacker to over-read or over-write NGINX worker memory resulting in its termination, using a specially crafted MP4 file. The issue only affects 32-bit NGINX Open Source if it is built with the ngx_http_mp4_module module and the mp4 directive is used in the configuration file. Additionally, the attack is possible only if an attacker can trigger the processing of a specially crafted MP4 file with the ngx_http_mp4_module module. 


Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX Open Source: affected 1.29.0 <1.29.7 (semver); affected 1.1.19 <1.28.3 (semver)

### CVE-2026-27944 — Nginx UI: Unauthenticated Backup Download with Encryption Key Disclosure
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-03-05 | Updated: 2026-03-19 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-311 CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data; CWE-306 CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. Prior to version 2.3.3, the /api/backup endpoint is accessible without authentication and discloses the encryption keys required to decrypt the backup in the X-Backup-Security response header. This allows an unauthenticated attacker to download a full system backup containing sensitive data (user credentials, session tokens, SSL private keys, Nginx configurations) and decrypt it immediately. This issue has been patched in version 2.3.3.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected < 2.3.3

References:
- https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/security/advisories/GHSA-g9w5-qffc-6762 [x_refsource_CONFIRM]

NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_mp4_module module, which might allow an attacker to trigger a buffer over-read or over-write to the NGINX worker memory resulting in its termination or possibly code execution, using a specially crafted MP4 file. This issue affects NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus if it is built with the ngx_http_mp4_module module and the mp4 directive is used in the configuration file. Additionally, the attack is possible only if an attacker can trigger the processing of a specially crafted MP4 file with the ngx_http_mp4_module module. 


Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. Prior to version 2.3.4, the nginx-ui configuration improperly handles URL-encoded traversal sequences. When specially crafted paths are supplied, the backend resolves them to the base Nginx configuration directory and executes the operation on the base directory (/etc/nginx). ### CVE-2026-33028 — Nginx UI: Race Condition Leads to Persistent Data Corruption and Service Collapse
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-03-30 | Updated: 2026-03-30 | Max CVSS: 7.1

- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.1 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:H/UI:N/VC:L/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. Prior to version 2.3.4, the nginx-ui application is vulnerable to a Race Condition. Due to the complete absence of synchronization mechanisms (Mutex) and non-atomic file writes, concurrent requests lead to the severe corruption of the primary configuration file (app.ini). This vulnerability results in a persistent Denial of Service (DoS) and introduces a non-deterministic path for Remote Code Execution (RCE) through configuration cross-contamination. This issue has been patched in version 2.3.4.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected < 2.3.4

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. In versions 2.3.3 and prior, Nginx-UI contains an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to access, modify, and delete resources belonging to other users. The application's base Model struct lacks a user_id field, and all resource endpoints perform queries by ID without verifying user ownership, enabling complete authorization bypass in multi-user environments. ### CVE-2026-33031 — Nginx-UI: Disabled users retain full API access through previously issued bearer tokens
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-04-20 | Updated: 2026-04-21 | Max CVSS: 8.6
- CWE: CWE-284 CWE-284: Improper Access Control; CWE-863 CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. Prior to version 2.3.4, a user who was disabled by an administrator can use previously issued API tokens for up to the token lifetime. In practice, disabling a compromised account does not actually terminate that user’s access, so an attacker who already stole a JWT can continue reading and modifying protected resources after the account is marked disabled. Since tokens can be used to create new accounts, it is possible the disabled user to maintain the privilege. Version 2.3.4 patches the issue.

Affected:

### CVE-2026-33032 — Nginx UI: Unauthenticated MCP Endpoint Allows Remote Nginx Takeover
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-03-30 | Updated: 2026-04-16 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-306 CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. In versions 2.3.5 and prior, the nginx-ui MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration exposes two HTTP endpoints: /mcp and /mcp_message. While /mcp requires both IP whitelisting and authentication (AuthRequired() middleware), the /mcp_message endpoint only applies IP whitelisting - and the default IP whitelist is empty, which the middleware treats as "allow all". This means any network attacker can invoke all MCP tools without authentication, including restarting nginx, creating/modifying/deleting nginx configuration files, and triggering automatic config reloads - achieving complete nginx service takeover. At time of publication, there are no publicly available patches.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected <= 2.3.5

### CVE-2026-34403 — Nginx-UI vulnerable to Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH) via missing origin validation on all WebSocket endpoints
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-04-20 | Updated: 2026-04-21 | Max CVSS: 5.5

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. Prior to version 2.3.5, all WebSocket endpoints in nginx-ui use a gorilla/websocket Upgrader with CheckOrigin unconditionally returning true, allowing Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH). Combined with the fact that authentication tokens are stored in browser cookies (set via JavaScript without HttpOnly or explicit SameSite attributes), a malicious webpage can establish authenticated WebSocket connections to the nginx-ui instance when a logged-in administrator visits the attacker-controlled page. Version 2.3.5 patches the issue.

Affected:

Nginx Proxy Manager versions 2.9.14 through 2.15.1, fixed in commit a5db5ed, contain an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability via OS command injection in the setupCertbotPlugins() function in backend/setup.js, allowing attackers with certificates:manage permission to execute arbitrary commands by storing a malicious payload in the dns_provider_credentials field. ### CVE-2026-42055 — NGINX ngx_http_proxy_v2_module and ngx_http_grpc_module vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-06-17 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122 Heap-based Buffer Overflow; CWE-131 Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_proxy_v2_module and ngx_http_grpc_module modules. This vulnerability exists when the proxy_http_version to 2 or grpc_pass directives are used to proxy HTTP/2 traffic, the ignore_invalid_headers directive is set to off, and the large_client_header_buffers directive size is larger than 2 megabytes. A remote, unauthenticated attacker, along with conditions beyond their control, could send large headers while creating an upstream request. This may cause a heap-based buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. 


Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

### CVE-2026-42220 — nginx-ui: Authenticated settings disclosure exposes node.secret and enables trusted-node authentication abuse, backup exfiltration, and restore-based nginx-ui state rollback
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-05-04 | Updated: 2026-05-06 | Max CVSS: 6.5
- CWE: CWE-200 CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor; CWE-863 CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 6.5 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. Prior to version 2.3.8, an authenticated user can call GET /api/settings and retrieve sensitive configuration values, including node.secret. The same node.secret is accepted by AuthRequired() through the X-Node-Secret header (or node_secret query parameter), causing the request to be treated as authenticated via the trusted-node path and associated with the init user. This issue has been patched in version 2.3.8.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected < 2.3.8

- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-05-04 | Updated: 2026-05-05 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-306 CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. From version 2.0.0 to before version 2.3.8, an unauthenticated network attacker can claim the initial administrator account on a fresh nginx-ui instance during the first-run setup window. The public /api/install endpoint is reachable without authentication, and the request-encryption flow only protects payload confidentiality in transit; it does not authenticate who is allowed to perform installation. A remote attacker who reaches the service before the legitimate operator can set the admin email, username, and password, causing permanent initial-instance takeover. This issue has been patched in version 2.3.8.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected >= 2.0.0, < 2.3.8

### CVE-2026-42223 — nginx-ui: Settings API Exposes Protected Secrets
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-05-04 | Updated: 2026-05-05 | Max CVSS: 6.5
- CWE: CWE-200 CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 6.5 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. Prior to version 2.3.8, the GetSettings API handler (api/settings/settings.go:24-65) serializes all settings structs to JSON and returns them to authenticated users. Many sensitive fields are tagged with protected:"true" - however, this tag is only enforced during writes (via ProtectedFill in SaveSettings) and is completely ignored during reads. This exposes 40+ protected fields including JwtSecret (enabling auth token forgery), NodeSecret (enabling cluster node impersonation), OIDC ClientSecret (enabling OAuth account takeover), and the IP whitelist configuration. This issue has been patched in version 2.3.8.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected < 2.3.8

References:
- https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/security/advisories/GHSA-q4w7-56hr-83rm [x_refsource_CONFIRM]
- https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/releases/tag/v2.3.8 [x_refsource_MISC]

### CVE-2026-42238 — Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Backup Restore in nginx-ui
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-05-04 | Updated: 2026-05-05 | Max CVSS: 9
- CWE: CWE-94 CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. Prior to version 2.3.8, nginx-ui exposes a backup restore endpoint (POST /api/restore) that is completely unauthenticated during the first 10 minutes after process startup on any fresh installation. An unauthenticated remote attacker can upload a crafted backup archive that overwrites the application's configuration file (app.ini) and SQLite database. Because the attacker controls the restored app.ini, they can inject an arbitrary OS command into the TestConfigCmd setting. After the application automatically restarts to apply the restored config, a single follow-up request triggers that command as the user running nginx-ui — typically root in Docker deployments. This issue has been patched in version 2.3.8.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected < 2.3.8

References:
- https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/security/advisories/GHSA-4pvg-prr3-9cxr [x_refsource_CONFIRM]
- https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/releases/tag/v2.3.8 [x_refsource_MISC]

NGINX Open Source has a vulnerability in the ngx_http_v3_module module. When NGINX Open Source is configured to use the HTTP/3 QUIC module, a remote unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can use a specially crafted HTTP/3 session to reopen a QPACK encoder stream. ### CVE-2026-42533 — NGINX Map directive and Regex matching vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-07-15 | Updated: 2026-11-03 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122 Heap-based Buffer Overflow
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A vulnerability exists in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when a map directive uses regex matching and a string expression references the map's regex capture variables before referencing the map output variable. Alternatively, the same result could be achieved by using a non-cacheable variable in a string expression under certain conditions. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




 Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX Plus: affected 37.0.0.1 <37.0.3.1 (custom); affected R36 <R36 P7 (custom); affected R33 <* (custom)
- F5 / NGINX Open Source: affected 1.31.2 <1.31.3 (custom); affected 0.9.6 <1.30.4 (custom)

### CVE-2026-44015 — Nginx UI: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via Cluster Proxy Middleware Allows Access to Internal Services
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-05-12 | Updated: 2026-05-14 | Max CVSS: 8.5
- CWE: CWE-918 CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. In 2.3.4 and earlier, an authenticated user can perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) by creating a cluster node pointing to an arbitrary internal URL and then sending API requests with the X-Node-ID header. The Proxy middleware forwards these requests to the attacker-specified internal address, bypassing network segmentation and enabling access to services bound to localhost or internal networks.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected <= 2.3.4

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as the data plane for NGINX Gateway Fabric, an injection vulnerability exists in the NGINX configuration generator component of NGINX Gateway Fabric. User-supplied string values from the NginxProxy Custom Resource Definition (CRD) access log format setting are rendered directly into NGINX configuration templates without sanitization or escaping. An authenticated attacker with permission to create or modify these CRDs may craft values that inject arbitrary NGINX configuration directives. When NGINX Ingress Controller processes Ingress or TransportServer resources, an authenticated, remote attacker with permission to create or modify Ingress or TransportServer resources can cause the NGINX Ingress Controller process to terminate. 



Impact:

This vulnerability allows a remote, authenticated attacker with at least Ingress or TransportServer resource write access to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX Ingress Controller system. There is no data plane exposure; this is a control plane issue only.

### CVE-2026-61628 — nginx ignition has Unauthenticated Admin Account Creation via Onboarding Race Condition
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-09-21 | Updated: 2026-09-21 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-362 CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

nginx ignition is a user interface for the nginx web server. Prior to version 2.41.1, `POST /api/users/onboarding/finish` is registered as anonymous (unauthenticated) and creates a user with full ReadWrite admin permissions. Because the handler uses a check-then-act (TOCTOU) pattern between the "onboarding already completed?" check and the user-creation write, with no atomic guard, a remote unauthenticated attacker who can reach an instance in its pre-onboarding state can create an administrator account for themselves — and concurrent requests can create multiple admin accounts in a single race. Version 2.41.1 patches the issue.

Affected:
- lucasdillmann / nginx-ignition: affected < 2.41.1

### CVE-2026-61629 — nginx ignition has  ParseAcceptLanguage `_` separator bypass that enables ~75x CPU amplification via Accept-Language header in i18nMiddleware
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-09-21 | Updated: 2026-09-24 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

nginx ignition is a user interface for the nginx web server. In versions 2.29.0 through 2.40.0, the gin i18n middleware in nginx-ignition's API server runs in front of every HTTP request and calls `golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage` on the raw `Accept-Language` header without imposing any size or shape filter. The underlying parser has quadratic-time behaviour on long lists of malformed language tags. The CVE-2022-32149 guard that golang.org/x/text added in v0.3.8 caps the number of `-` characters in the input at 1000, but it does not cap `_` characters even though the parser's internal scanner aliases `_` to `-` before parsing. A single unauthenticated GET request with an `Accept-Language` header built out of `_` separators burns about 2.4 seconds of server CPU on the host running nginx-ignition; ten concurrent attackers saturate a ten-core box for the duration of the attack while consuming ~10 MiB/s of upstream bandwidth. Version 2.40.1 fixes this issue.

Affected:
- lucasdillmann / nginx-ignition: affected >= 2.29.0, < 2.40.1

- https://github.com/lucasdillmann/nginx-ignition/security/advisories/GHSA-jr34-h97m-9hpx [x_refsource_CONFIRM]

### CVE-2026-78689 — NGINX ngx_http_js_module vulnerablility
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-09-02 | Updated: 2026-09-03 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Description


NGINX JavaScript (njs) has a vulnerability in the XML module's namespace prefix list parser, reachable through the xml.exclusiveC14n() method. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger it when an affected NGINX configuration passes an externally controlled XML namespace prefix list to that method. Both the njs and the QuickJS (qjs) engines are affected. A crafted prefix list causes an out-of-bounds write past the end of a heap allocation. With the njs engine, which is the engine used when the js_engine directive is absent, this corrupts adjacent objects and crashes the NGINX worker. With the QuickJS engine, the same call additionally leaks the prefix list on every invocation, causing worker memory to grow across requests. The official nginxinc/nginx-saml reference implementation is affected during SAML signature verification. It reads InclusiveNamespaces/@PrefixList from an untrusted SAML message and passes it to xml.exclusiveC14n() before the signature has been verified, so a valid SAML signature is not required. A crafted SAML Response, Assertion, LogoutRequest, or LogoutResponse is sufficient. Code execution has not been demonstrated and cannot be ruled out for all platforms, as the effect of the out-of-bounds write depends on conditions beyond the attacker's control.  








 Impact


This vulnerability allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service on the NGINX system, either through repeatable worker restarts or through worker memory growth or possibly trigger code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** None

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX JavaScript: affected 0.7.10 <1.0.1 (custom)

Credits: F5 acknowledges Vladimir Tokarev of Cyera and Sujal Tuladhar (EvilGenius) for bringing this issue to our attention and following the highest standards of coordinated disclosure.

Prior to 2.4.1, internal/config/validation.go (ValidateConfigFile) is a security control that blocks dangerous nginx directives — js_*, perl_*, load_module of the njs/perl modules, and user root. It is enforced on three of the four config-write paths: api/config/add.go, api/config/modify.go, and mcp/config/config_modify.go. The fourth path — the MCP tool nginx_config_add (mcp/config/config_add.go) — does NOT call it: it writes the caller-supplied content straight to disk and reloads nginx. An authenticated MCP caller (or an MCP agent induced via prompt injection) can therefore inject exactly the directives the control is meant to block, leading to nginx code execution on deployments where the njs/perl module is available (e.g. the official Docker image). This issue is fixed in version 2.4.1.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected < 2.4.1

### CVE-2026-84318 — Nginx UI: MCP `nginx_config_add` Bypasses Directive Validation — Authenticated RCE
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-10-12 | Updated: 2026-10-13 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-693 CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. From 2.0.0-rc.6 until 2.4.1, the MCP tool nginx_config_add writes nginx configuration files to disk and triggers an nginx reload without calling config.ValidateConfigFile. The identical flow in the REST API (POST /api/configs) does call that function and correctly rejects dangerous directives. An authenticated attacker can exploit this gap to write config files containing any blocked directive (perl, js_import, load_module, user root, etc.), bypassing nginx-ui's entire security layer. On a server with the nginx Perl, njs, or Lua module loaded, this is post-authentication Remote Code Execution. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.1.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected >= 2.0.0-rc.6, < 2.4.1

### CVE-2026-84321 — Nginx UI: Standalone short tokens survive administrative revocation in cache and authenticate again after account re-enable
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-10-12 | Updated: 2026-10-13 | Max CVSS: 5.4
- CWE: CWE-613 CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 5.4 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. Prior to 2.4.1, GenerateShortToken creates standalone short-token records without a long Token value, but DeleteUserTokens invalidates cached entries only when the long Token field is nonempty. A revoked short token can therefore remain in the short_token cache and authenticate again if the associated account is re-enabled before the cache entry expires because GetTokenUserByShortToken reads the surviving entry, restoring access to HTTP or WebSocket routes that accept short-token authentication. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.1.

Affected:
- 0xJacky / nginx-ui: affected < 2.4.1

### CVE-2026-91184 — NGINX Gateway Fabric vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-10-14 | Updated: 2026-10-15 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-76 CWE-76
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Description

NGINX Gateway Fabric has a vulnerability when it renders the spec.basic.realm (and spec.jwt.realm) field of a namespaced AuthenticationFilter verbatim, unescaped and unvalidated, into the shared data-plane nginx.conf as auth_basic "<realm>";. A namespaced authenticated attacker that configures AuthenticationFilter CRD to an HTTPRoute/GRPCRoute on a shared Gateway can craft a realm value that closes the quoted directive and the enclosing location {} block and injects arbitrary NGINX directives into that Gateway's data-plane config. 

Impact

A remote authenticated attacker can send crafted requests to configure NGINX Gateway Fabric AuthenticationFilter CRD and may be able to read every co-located tenant's mounted secrets, SSRF via proxy_pass, reading the pod ServiceAccount token, or hijacking other tenants' routes. There is no data plane exposure; this is a control plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** As this attack is conducted by authenticated users with Kubernetes Role-based Access Control (RBAC) write access to AuthenticationFilter CRD and Secrets, the only complete mitigation is to restrict that access to fully trusted administrators only.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX Gateway Fabric: affected 2.4.0 <2.8.0 (custom)

Credits: F5 acknowledges apvxlab (AppViewX security research) for bringing this issue to our attention and following the highest standards of coordinated disclosure.

References:
- https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000162609 [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-93479 — NGINX map directive and regex matching vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-10-14 | Updated: 2026-10-29 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122 Heap-based Buffer Overflow
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A vulnerability exists in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when a map directive uses regex matching and the root directive or access log format references the map's regex capture variables before referencing the map output variable. Alternatively, the same result could be achieved by using a non-cacheable variable in a string expression under certain conditions. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** To mitigate this vulnerability, do not use unnamed captures. Use named captures instead and limit their usage to the block with the regex match.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX Plus: affected 37.1.0 <37.1.0.1 (custom); affected 37.0.0 <37.0.5.1 (custom); affected R36 <* (custom); affected R35 <* (custom); affected R34 <* (custom); affected R33 <* (custom)

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers 

unauthenticated

 access to protected 

paths. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.

### CVE-2026-97629 — NGINX ngx_http_ssl_module vulnerability

Description
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with ssl_session_cache 

shared:name:size

without an explicit ssl_session_ticket_key file directives to automatically rotate SSL session ticket keys, a remote unauthenticated attacker is able to forge client SSL sessions 

in a non-deterministic manner that is beyond the attacker's control. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates.

Impact


This vulnerability can lead to the exposure of resources or functionality to unintended actors, possibly providing attackers with access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** Do not enable automatic rotation of SSL session ticket keys: 

option a) remove the "ssl_session_cache shared:name:size" directive;

option b) switch to loading static ticket keys from a file using the "ssl_session_ticket_key" directive.
 https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_ssl_module.html#ssl_session_ticket_key  

Systems that disable session tickets ("ssl_session_tickets off;") are not affected.
 https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_ssl_module.html#ssl_session_tickets

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Description
NGINX JavaScript (njs) has a vulnerability where the njs XML module exposes entity-backed XML attributes inconsistently with libxml2 canonicalization. In both the built-in njs and QuickJS backends during the canonicalization process, the $attr$Name getter may return undefined for an explicitly present attribute containing an internal entity reference. The $attrs getter may return a value derived only from the first attribute child. This may allow an unauthenticated attacker that invests significant effort in obtaining a genuinely signed document to skip validation while signature verification succeeds. An nginx-saml deployment is a confirmed affected consumer when run with the built-in njs backend.

Impact
In affected signed-XML consumers, an unauthenticated attacker can cause security-relevant attributes to appear absent or truncated while signature verification succeeds. In nginx-saml, this can bypass expiry, Destination, and request-correlation checks, enabling replay or acceptance of a response outside its intended context. It does not permit signature or identity forgery, or a direct availability impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



 Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** Applications processing signed XML should reject DTD-bearing input before calling xml.parse(). The check must cover the complete document after decoding its accepted input encoding; a parser-level DTD prohibition is preferable to a raw byte search for "<!DOCTYPE". 

Applications should also treat absent security-relevant attributes as validation failures rather than optional values. nginx-saml deployments should explicitly validate Destination, request correlation when unsolicited SSO is not intended, assertion validity, bearer SubjectConfirmation, Recipient, and SubjectConfirmationData InResponseTo.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX JavaScript: affected 0.7.10 <1.0.2 (custom)

Credits: F5

References:
- https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000162615 [vendor-advisory]

Nginx UI is a web user interface for the Nginx web server. - SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. As a result, the worker process stops accepting new connections and processing existing connections. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Impact: This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) of NGINX. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** None.

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX Open Source: affected 1.31.0 <1.31.9 (semver); affected 1.30.0 <1.30.7 (semver); affected 1.31.0 <* (semver)
- F5 / NGINX Plus: affected 37.2.0.1 <37.2.1.1 (custom); affected 37.0.0 <37.0.8.1 (custom); affected R33 <* (custom)

Credits: F5

References:
- https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163930 [vendor-advisory,patch]

- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-11-18 | Updated: 2026-11-19 | Max CVSS: 9.2

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** None

- F5 / NGINX Plus: affected 37.1.0 <37.3.0.1 (custom); affected 37.0.0 <37.0.8.1 (custom); affected R33 <* (custom)

### CVE-2026-123634 — NGINX resolver vulnerability
- Assigner: f5 | Published: 2026-11-18 | Updated: 2026-11-19 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE)



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

**workarounds:** Avoid using SSI or mirror directives and avoid configuring a proxied server name with variables

Affected:
- F5 / NGINX Plus: affected 37.1.0 <37.3.0.1 (custom); affected 37.0.0 <37.0.8.1 (custom); affected R33 <* (custom)
- F5 / NGINX Open Source: affected 1.31.0 <1.31.9 (semver); affected 1.30.0 <1.30.7 (semver); affected 0.6.18 <* (semver)

Credits: F5 acknowledges Xint.io for bringing this issue to our attention and following the highest standards of coordinated disclosure.

References:
- https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163925 [vendor-advisory,patch]

### CVE-2026-129171 — NginxPulse 1.5.0 before 1.6.26 SQL Injection via /api/stats/:type
- Assigner: VulnCheck | Published: 2026-11-13 | Updated: 2026-11-18 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-89 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

NginxPulse 1.5.0 before 1.6.26 contains an unauthenticated sql injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to append SQL via the id and locationType parameters of /api/stats/:type. Attackers can close the quoted table-name identifier and use error-based output to read database contents, and read or write server files via PostgreSQL superuser functions.

Affected:
- likaia / NginxPulse: affected 1.5.0 <1.6.26 (semver)
